Environmental law prohibits actions that threaten species survival.
laws.penalty: Fine; mandatory reforestation; up to 8 years for commercial-scale species habitat destruction
exceptions: Licensed activities within approved environmental impact assessments

quiz.q: What is the Gran Chaco significance in South America?
options: The second largest forest in South America after the Amazon with exceptional biodiversity
quiz.explanation: The Gran Chaco is South Americas second largest forest — extending across Paraguay, Argentina, and Bolivia — with exceptional biodiversity including species found nowhere else globally.

laws.title: Privacy Violations and Surveillance
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized monitoring or data collection
laws.fullDescription: Paraguay criminal code prohibits unauthorized surveillance, wiretapping, and personal data collection. Government surveillance of political opponents has been a concern. Civil society organizations monitor for surveillance abuses particularly in politically polarized periods.
laws.penalty: 2 to 5 years imprisonment
exceptions: Judicial orders authorizing surveillance in criminal investigations

quiz.q: What concern has been raised about surveillance in Paraguay political context?
options: Government surveillance of political opponents during polarized periods
quiz.explanation: Paraguay history of political polarization has generated concerns about unauthorized surveillance — monitoring of political opponents, journalists, and civil society using state intelligence resources.

laws.title: Crimes Against Indigenous Peoples
laws.subtitle: Persecution and dispossession of indigenous communities
laws.fullDescription: Paraguay has significant indigenous populations whose territories face encroachment from agricultural expansion. The criminal code addresses persecution, forced displacement, and theft of ancestral lands from indigenous communities. INDI (indigenous affairs institute) monitors rights violations.
laws.penalty: Varies by underlying offense; indigenous targeting adds aggravating factor
exceptions: None for crimes specifically targeting indigenous communities
laws.sourceLabel: Paraguay Criminal Code; Indigenous Rights Law 904

quiz.q: What institution monitors indigenous rights violations in Paraguay?
quiz.explanation: INDI (Instituto Nacional del Indigena) monitors rights violations against Paraguay indigenous peoples and coordinates legal protections and land titling for indigenous communities throughout the country.

laws.title: Illegal Well Drilling
laws.subtitle: Unauthorized extraction from the Guarani Aquifer
laws.fullDescription: Paraguay overlies part of the Guarani Aquifer and unauthorized well drilling for agricultural or industrial extraction beyond permitted volumes is regulated by ERSSAN. Illegal wells can deplete the aquifer and contaminate groundwater through improper casing.
laws.penalty: Fine; well sealing order; extraction permit suspension
exceptions: Registered domestic wells within approved parameters
laws.sourceLabel: Paraguay Water Code — ERSSAN; Guarani Aquifer Treaty

quiz.q: What regulatory body oversees water extraction from Paraguay groundwater?
quiz.explanation: ERSSAN (Ente Regulador de Servicios Sanitarios) oversees water and sanitation services in Paraguay including regulation of groundwater extraction to protect the Guarani Aquifer from over-extraction.

laws.title: Illegal Lottery and Numbers Operations
laws.subtitle: Running unauthorized lottery schemes
laws.fullDescription: Illegal lottery operations — particularly the informal numbers game (la quiniela informal) — operate outside official licensing in Paraguay. While the state lottery is authorized, unauthorized competing operations evade taxes and consumer protection requirements.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 1 year imprisonment for operators
laws.sourceLabel: Paraguay Gambling Law — CONAJZAR; Lottery Regulation

quiz.q: What informal lottery game operates outside official licensing in Paraguay?
options: La quiniela informal — an unauthorized numbers game
quiz.explanation: La quiniela informal — an unlicensed numbers game operated by informal bookmakers — is the most common unauthorized lottery operation in Paraguay, competing with the state lottery while evading taxes and consumer protections.

laws.title: Explosives Crimes
laws.subtitle: Using explosives in criminal activities
laws.fullDescription: Paraguay mining and quarrying industry provides legal access to explosives. Criminal misuse of explosives — in social conflict incidents and criminal operations — is criminalized with severe penalties. EPP guerrillas have used improvised explosive devices in attacks on security forces.
laws.penalty: 8 to 15 years imprisonment; enhanced if harm results
exceptions: Licensed mining and construction use within strict operational parameters

quiz.q: What group has used improvised explosive devices against security forces in Paraguay?
options: No group uses explosives in Paraguay
EPP (Ejercito del Pueblo Paraguayo) guerrillas in northern departments
quiz.explanation: The EPP guerrilla organization has used improvised explosive devices — including landmines and booby traps — in attacks against Paraguayan security forces conducting anti-EPP operations in northern departments.

laws.title: Construction Fraud
laws.subtitle: Charging for construction work not performed
laws.fullDescription: Construction fraud — collecting payment for projects not completed, using substandard materials, and building without required permits — affects both private clients and government contracting. Government infrastructure fraud drains public resources through phantom projects.
laws.penalty: Fine; up to 5 years for government project fraud; restitution

quiz.q: What form of construction fraud most affects Paraguay government projects?
options: Phantom projects — receiving payment for infrastructure never built
quiz.explanation: Phantom projects — receiving government payment for infrastructure projects never actually constructed — are the most costly form of construction fraud in Paraguay, draining public resources through corrupt procurement processes.

laws.title: Chaco Jaguar Corridor Destruction
laws.subtitle: Eliminating the transnational jaguar habitat corridor
laws.fullDescription: The Gran Chaco forms a critical jaguar habitat corridor connecting populations across Paraguay, Argentina, Bolivia, and Brazil. Deforestation fragmenting this corridor threatens jaguar viability. Environmental law prohibits habitat destruction in designated jaguar corridor areas.
laws.penalty: Fine; mandatory reforestation; up to 7 years for commercial corridor destruction
exceptions: Authorized activities with wildlife corridor mitigation plans
laws.sourceLabel: Paraguay Environmental Law — Jaguar Corridor Protection

quiz.q: Why is the Gran Chaco jaguar corridor regionally significant?
options: It connects jaguar populations across Paraguay, Argentina, Bolivia, and Brazil
quiz.explanation: The Gran Chaco jaguar corridor is regionally critical — connecting jaguar populations across four countries. Fragmentation of this corridor by deforestation isolates populations, reducing genetic diversity and threatening long-term jaguar survival.

laws.title: Gang-Related Murder
laws.subtitle: Organized gang killings linked to drug territory
laws.fullDescription: Gang-related murders — killings linked to drug territory disputes, trafficking enforcement, and criminal organization conflicts — have increased in Paraguay as organized crime has grown. Aggravated murder charges apply to gang-related killings with enhanced sentences.
laws.penalty: 20 to 30 years imprisonment for gang-related aggravated murder
laws.sourceLabel: Paraguay Criminal Code — Aggravated Murder; Organized Crime

quiz.q: What underlying conflict drives most gang-related murders in Paraguay?
options: Drug territory disputes and trafficking route control between rival organizations
quiz.explanation: Drug territory disputes — rival criminal organizations fighting for control of cannabis production areas, trafficking routes, and distribution networks — are the primary driver of gang-related murders in Paraguay.
